findings.claim: The BeamNG engine binary links Draco and Assimp and includes meshoptimizer simplification. Loading glTF/.glb shapes requires the `-assimp` command-line flag.
findings.evidence: Local: `ldd BinLinux/BeamNG.drive.x64` → libassimp.so.6, libdraco.so.9. `strings` shows 'glTF shapes require the -assimp flag: {}', '*.glb', 'Failed to load glTF shape: {}', 'meshopt_simplify', 'meshopt_simplifySloppy', 'reloadStaticCollision'.

findings.claim: BeamNG vehicle physics are computed in local per-vehicle space, so they are immune to distance from the origin. Graphics jitter far from the origin was the remaining problem. In Oct 2024 devs rejected switching to doubles, stabilised the camera first, and added a CLI flag to shift everything 500 km away for testing. Users report the issue was effectively fixed around v0.34.
findings.evidence: estama (BeamNG Team, 2020-09-09): 'Our vehicle physics are always calculated in a local to each vehicle space… The same does not apply for the GFX subsystem' https://www.beamng.com/posts/1327487/ ; tdev (2024-10-15): 'We will not switch to doubles for everything… We now added a command line argument to shift everything into 500km away' https://www.beamng.com/threads/double-precision-float.96528/page-2 ; users, Oct 2025, on page-3. I did not find the official changelog entry.

findings.claim: Float32 position step (ulp) is 0.06 mm at 1 km, 0.5 mm at 8 km, 3.9 mm at 65 km, 3 cm at 500 km and 0.5 m at Earth-radius scale (6.4e6 m). ECEF or planet-centred coordinates therefore cannot be used directly in a float32 engine, and a local origin within tens of km of the player is needed.
findings.evidence: Computed with numpy.spacing(float32(x)) in scratchpad

findings.claim: Curvature drop below the tangent plane is d²/(2R): 0.08 m at 1 km, 0.31 m at 2 km, 0.71 m at 3 km, 1.96 m at 5 km, 7.85 m at 10 km, 31 m at 20 km, 196 m at 50 km. The geometric horizon for a 1.5 m eye height is about 4.4 km (35.7 km at 100 m altitude). Curvature is irrelevant for physics near the car but visible in distant LOD rings.
findings.evidence: Computed with R=6371008.8 m (exact R - sqrt(R²-d²) matches to <1 mm below 20 km)

findings.claim: In the 3D Tiles spec, geometricError is in metres, and REPLACE vs ADD refinement, region/box/sphere bounding volumes, and WGS84 ECEF (EPSG:4978) coordinates are standard. glTF 2.0 is the primary content format, and implicit quadtree/octree tiling exists.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/CesiumGS/3d-tiles/blob/main/specification/README.adoc

findings.claim: CesiumJS computes screen-space error as geometricError*height/(distance*sseDenominator), where sseDenominator = 2*tan(fovy/2). The default maximumScreenSpaceError is 16 px and the default cacheBytes is 512 MiB.
findings.evidence: Cesium main: packages/engine/Source/Scene/Cesium3DTile.js:955-993 `error = (geometricError * height) / (distance * sseDenominator);`; Cesium 1.120 Core/PerspectiveFrustum.js:204 `frustum._sseDenominator = 2.0 * Math.tan(0.5 * frustum._fovy);`; Cesium3DTileset.js:252 `options.maximumScreenSpaceError ?? 16`, :255 `options.cacheBytes ?? 512*1024*1024`

findings.claim: Cesium for Unreal and Unity anchor the engine world to a georeference origin (lat/lon/height or ECEF) with a local East-Up-North frame. An origin-shift component moves that origin with the camera and keeps the globe's local up on the engine's up axis. GlobeAnchor components keep double-precision global positions for objects. Cesium staff note that UE5 LWC reduces the need for continuous rebasing, and sub-level-based switching is the recommended pattern.
findings.evidence: https://cesium.com/learn/cesium-unreal/ref-doc/CesiumOriginShiftComponent_8h.html ('to keep the globe's local "up" direction aligned with the +Z axis'); https://cesium.com/learn/unity/unity-placing-objects/ ('different parts of the world have local reference frames with conflicting "up" directions'); https://community.cesium.com/t/cesium-origin-shift/31378

findings.claim: MSFS 2020 (Asobo) uses a Mercator quadtree from the Bing tile system and accepts polar stretching. It recursively requests frustum tiles by estimated screen size and measured bandwidth, and draws with parent data while children load. It uses skirts and index-buffer variants for cracks, double-precision CPU positions, an inverted depth buffer, and an 'anchor space' with origin at the camera and Y along the surface normal. 1.5 billion buildings were AI-generated by Blackshark from 2D imagery, with photogrammetry for about 400 cities.
findings.evidence: Asobo 'Designing Terrain System' (Lionel Fuentes) PDF https://www.asobostudio.com/files/inline-images/Designing_Terrain_System_Fuentes_Lionel.pdf. Slides: 'Quadtree / Mercator projection / Stretches at the poles / Not ideal but the vast majority of available data uses it'; 'Requested LoD depends on: Estimated tile screen size, Estimated available network bandwidth'; 'CPU node position Float 32 bits → Double 64 bits; GPU: Inverted depth buffer, Introduce « anchor space »; Origin = camera position; Y = Earth surface normal'. Blackshark: https://techcrunch.com/2020/08/17/meet-the-startup-that-helped-microsoft-build-the-world-of-flight-simulator

findings.claim: Outerra uses a cube mapped to a sphere (faces of about 10,000 km), a wavelet-compressed base DEM, and GPU fractal refinement down to cm scale. A separate local coordinate system fades in around level 18 to beat precision limits. It also uses a logarithmic depth buffer: gl_Position.z = 2.0*log(gl_Position.w*C + 1)/log(far*C + 1) - 1.
findings.evidence: https://outerra.blogspot.com/2012/11/maximizing-depth-buffer-range-and.html (formula verified). The cube-face size and level-18 local frame come from search-result summaries of Outerra forum/moddb posts (pages themselves were login-gated or returned 403).

findings.claim: Google Earth's native 'rocktree' format is an octree of OBB-bounded nodes (PlanetoidMetadata → BulkMetadata → NodeData meshes + JPG/CRN textures). It has no 2D projection, so there is no pole problem.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/retroplasma/earth-reverse-engineering (archived)

findings.claim: KSP keeps the world origin on the active vessel (FloatingOrigin + Krakensbane, which also absorbs frame velocity; added in v0.17). Planet terrain uses PQS (Procedural Quad Sphere), a cube-sphere quadtree, which KSP2 kept on compute shaders.
findings.evidence: KSP API https://www.kerbalspaceprogram.com/ksp/api/class_krakensbane.html ; forum https://forum.kerbalspaceprogram.com/topic/207101-question-on-krakensbane ('making sure the world origin stays centered on the active vessel'); PQS via search summaries of the KSP forum and the KSP2 dev diary.

findings.claim: UE5 Large World Coordinates use doubles in core types and Chaos physics; the default WORLD_MAX is 88 million km. Niagara stays float, splitting the world into cells plus a local offset.
findings.evidence: https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/large-world-coordinates-in-unreal-engine-5

findings.claim: S2 is 6 cube faces projected to the sphere with a nonlinear warp and Hilbert-curve 64-bit cell IDs, levels 0-30 (~1 cm). Max/min cell area is about 2.1x at every level. Level 13 is about 1 km, level 15 about 250-300 m, level 17 about 70 m, level 20 about 9 m. 3D Tiles has an official 3DTILES_bounding_volume_S2 extension with implicit quadtree/octree subdivision.
findings.evidence: http://s2geometry.io/devguide/s2cell_hierarchy.html ; http://s2geometry.io/resources/s2cell_statistics.html ; https://github.com/CesiumGS/3d-tiles/tree/main/extensions/3DTILES_bounding_volume_S2

findings.claim: HEALPix is equal-area and iso-latitude with 12 base pixels and is optimised for spherical-harmonic analysis. Its diamond and polar-cap cell shapes and lack of game/GIS tooling make it a poor fit for terrain tiles. A normalised cube concentrates area at face centres; a tangent (atan) warp or the S2 quadratic warp fixes most of it. Dimitrijević/Lambers/Rančić (2016) compare cube-map projections for planet terrain.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HEALPix ; https://redblobgames.com/x/1938-square-tiling-of-sphere ; https://casopisi.junis.ni.ac.rs/index.php/FUMathInf/article/view/871

findings.claim: Web Mercator (Bing/Google/OSM XYZ) clips latitude at ±85.05112878°. Ground resolution scales with cos(lat), so tiles near the poles cover tiny areas and the poles are missing. This is the source of the 'polar warping' the user wants to avoid. Bing Maps for Enterprise is retired for free (Basic) accounts; Enterprise accounts run until 30 June 2028.
findings.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/bingmaps/articles/bing-maps-tile-system

findings.claim: Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles: the root is https://tile.googleapis.com/v1/3dtiles/root.json?key=KEY. Child URIs are relative and must carry `session` and `key`, and one root request covers at least 3 h of tile requests. Billing is per root request (Enterprise SKU: 1,000 free/month, then $6 per 1,000). Limits are 10,000 roots/day and 12,000 QPM; renderer tile requests are not quota-limited. Each tile's glTF asset.copyright must be aggregated, sorted by frequency and shown with the Google logo. Tiles are ECEF glTF (.glb).
findings.evidence: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/3d-tiles ; https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/create-renderer ; https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/usage-and-billing ; https://developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/pricing ; per-root billing: https://mapsplatform.google.com/resources/blog/build-immersive-maps-at-scale-with-photorealistic-3d-2d-and-street-view-tiles-now-in-ga/

findings.claim: Google Map Tiles API policies forbid pre-fetching, indexing, storing or caching content beyond honouring Cache-Control max-age/stale-while-revalidate, and forbid offline use and geodata extraction. 3D overlays must not be 'extracted, traced, or otherwise derived by hand or machine from Photorealistic 3D Tiles'. Baking Google meshes into a BeamNG level (the Blosm workflow) conflicts with these terms; live streaming with an HTTP-cache-compliant cache and attribution is the compliant shape.
findings.evidence: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/policies

findings.claim: Photorealistic 3D Tiles and 2D satellite tiles are not available (HTTP 403) for projects linked to an EEA billing address that were created after 8 July 2025, or that are no longer in the Unmodified State.
findings.evidence: https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/map-tiles

findings.claim: Open global data that is cacheable and redistributable: Copernicus DEM GLO-30/GLO-90 as COGs on s3://copernicus-dem-30m (a DSM, so it includes buildings and trees; no ocean tiles); AWS Terrain Tiles (Mapzen/Tilezen) Terrarium PNGs at https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png, z0-15, decode h = R*256 + G + B/256 - 32768; Mapterhorn planet.pmtiles (Terrarium, Europe-focused high-res); Overture buildings (ODbL, global, OSM + Microsoft + Google ML footprints, partial heights).
findings.evidence: https://registry.opendata.aws/copernicus-dem/ ; https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/ ; https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/formats.md ; https://protomaps.com/blog/mapterhorn-terrain/ ; https://docs.overturemaps.org/guides/buildings

findings.claim: Quantized-mesh (Cesium World Terrain format) uses a geographic EPSG:4326 TMS with 2 root tiles. The header has an ECEF centre, min/max height, a bounding sphere and a horizon-occlusion point. Vertices are zig-zag delta-encoded u, v, h in 0..32767, edge-index lists support skirts, and extensions add oct-normals and a water mask. It is a good wire format for a companion server feeding Lua.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/CesiumGS/quantized-mesh

findings.claim: Reference runtime streamers in other engines exist and are worth copying: 3DTilesRendererJS (NASA-AMMOS) with GoogleCloudAuthPlugin (session renewal), errorTarget (20 px for Google tiles) and an LRU cache with hard byte caps; and Godotiles/bevytiles/raytiles (Rust; Esri/Mapbox imagery + Terrarium DEM, adaptive quadtree z9-22, on-disk resumable cache, large-world shifting).
findings.evidence: https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/3DTilesRendererJS ; https://unpkg.com/3d-tiles-renderer@0.4.10/src/plugins/README.md ; https://store.godotengine.org/asset/ziv/godotiles/

findings.claim: Cesium ion can proxy Google 3D Tiles and Bing imagery. Its community plan includes 1,000 Google root tiles per month and 1,000 Bing/Google imagery sessions per month, limited to 5 Google root requests per IP per minute, and is for non-commercial use.
findings.evidence: https://cesium.com/platform/cesium-ion/pricing/ ; https://community.cesium.com/t/google-tiles-limitations/31034 (search-result summaries)

findings.claim: BeamMP distributes maps as client ZIPs in Resources/Client that every player downloads before joining. It has no map streaming, so multiplayer would need each client to stream the same tiles around a shared geodetic anchor.
findings.evidence: https://hosthavoc.com/wiki/game-servers/beammp/add-custom-map (and other host guides)

blockers: Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles ToS: no pre-fetching, storing or caching beyond HTTP Cache-Control; no offline use or extraction; the Google logo and per-tile attributions must be displayed. A 'bake to BeamNG level' approach, or a shared server cache of Google meshes, is non-compliant. Deriving collision meshes from Google tiles may count as forbidden 'derived' 3D content (unresolved legal question).
Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles return HTTP 403 for EEA-billed projects created after 8 July 2025. If the user or players are in the EEA, Google cannot be the primary source.
Each player must use their own Google API key plus billing account (1,000 free root sessions/month). Redistributing a shared key in a mod would expose it and break quotas.
BeamNG terrain (TerrainBlock) is limited to square, power-of-two 128-8192 grids, so it is useless as a global terrain. At most it can serve a near-field heightfield patch, re-generated on rebase.

Static collision rebuild (be:reloadCollision) appears to be global. Its cost when many streamed tiles are added or removed per second is unknown and could cause hitches. Profiling is needed, as is checking reloadStaticCollision and per-object collision options.
Loading glTF (.glb) shapes natively needs the -assimp launch flag; otherwise geometry must go through ProceduralMesh tables or be converted to DAE/cdae on the server.

Lua table-based ProceduralMesh creation for 100k+ triangle photogrammetry tiles may be CPU-heavy on the GE thread. Texture upload from runtime-downloaded JPEGs needs an investigated path (Material colorMap on a file written to the user folder).

Rendering far from the origin was only recently stabilised (~v0.34) and BeamNG has no public origin-shift API. The mod must implement its own rebasing: teleport vehicles, props, camera and all tiles together. Doing this mid-drive without disturbing physics or AI or replays is unproven.

Bing Maps free/basic access is retired; Esri World Imagery licensing for non-Esri game use is unclear. High-resolution open global imagery is scarce: Sentinel-2 is 10 m, and good orthophotos are country-specific.
recommendations: Architecture: a 'globe in the server, flat bubble in the game' model, copying MSFS anchor space and Cesium origin shifting. The companion server (Rust or Python) holds all positions in double-precision WGS84/ECEF. BeamNG only ever sees a local ENU frame anchored at a geodetic point (φ0, λ0, h0) near the player, with Z = ellipsoid up (BeamNG is Z-up).

Rebase the anchor when the player gets more than about 2-5 km from it. Rebuild the bubble, then translate vehicles, camera and existing tiles by the anchor delta in one frame, and rotate them too, since the up vector changes by about 0.009°/km. Keep the bubble radius at 10-20 km so float32 error stays below 1-2 mm (ulp is 0.5 mm at 8 km and 1 mm at 16 km).

Curvature: transform every vertex exactly as ECEF → ENU(anchor) in doubles on the server. The Earth then naturally curves away (−7.85 m at 10 km, −196 m at 50 km) and the horizon is correct with no approximation. Gravity stays the normal BeamNG −Z, which is correct within the bubble. obj:setPlanets exists but is unnecessary unless BeamNG's world is centred on the planet, which float32 rules out (0.5 m precision at 6.4e6 m).

Global tiling to avoid polar warping: index the server's own synthesized tiles (DEM mesh, OSM buildings, roads) with an S2-style cube-sphere quadtree (6 faces, quadratic or tangent warp, ~2.1x area variance). S2 level ≈ LOD: L13 ≈ 1 km, L15 ≈ 250 m, L17 ≈ 70 m, L20 ≈ 9 m. Resample Web-Mercator sources (Terrarium, Esri) into it on the server. Consume ECEF-native sources (Google 3D Tiles, quantized-mesh) as-is, since they have no projection.

LOD: implement Cesium-style SSE selection on the server or in Lua: sse = geometricError*screenH/(dist*2*tan(fov/2)), refine while sse > 16 px (raise to 20-32 for performance). Use REPLACE refinement, keep the parent visible until all children are loaded (as MSFS does), and hide cracks with skirts. Concentric rings for a first version: ~2-4 km of high detail with collision, then ~20 km of medium detail, then a horizon ring with no collision.

Collision only for the near field: give ProceduralMesh collision only to tiles within about 1-2 km of the vehicle(s). Far tiles render without collision. Batch collision rebuilds (one be:reloadCollision per batch, not per tile) and profile the cost early.

Data plan, MVP (fully open, cacheable, legal to cache on the server): terrain from Copernicus GLO-30 COGs plus Terrarium tiles for gaps; buildings from Overture/OSM footprints extruded by height, levels or a default; roads from OSM as decal roads or MeshRoad/ProceduralMesh with a terrain cut; imagery from Sentinel-2 cloudless or Esri where licensed.

Data plan, v2 'photoreal' mode: an optional, user-supplied Google Map Tiles API key; the server acts as a pure on-the-fly 3D Tiles client (ECEF glb → Draco decode → ENU transform → ProceduralMesh payload). Honour Cache-Control, store nothing persistently, show the Google logo and aggregated asset.copyright in a UI app, and fall back to open data for EEA users or users without a key.

Reuse BeamNG's own building blocks instead of inventing new ones: the ProceduralMesh pattern from techCore.placeObject; the cube-sphere code in flowgraph planet.lua as a reference only; util_terrainGenerator if a near-field TerrainBlock patch is wanted for terrain-material and ground-model physics; editor/terrainAndRoadImporter for road terraform logic.

Wire format server→game: a compact binary per tile, quantized-mesh-like (ENU-relative float32 or int16 positions, oct-normals, UVs, an index list, a texture ref), delivered over localhost HTTP or WebSocket. Decode in LuaJIT with FFI into tables for ProceduralMesh:createMesh. Write textures to the user folder for Material colorMap. Do the heavy work (Draco, reprojection, simplification with meshoptimizer, mesh merging) on the server, not in Lua.

Prototype order: (1) Lua bubble manager with anchor plus rebase on an empty level such as 'smallgrid'; (2) DEM-only terrain tiles via ProceduralMesh with curvature; (3) near-field collision and profiling; (4) OSM buildings and roads; (5) imagery; (6) the optional Google 3D Tiles mode.

research.topic: Online data sources for streaming Earth at runtime into BeamNG.Earth: capabilities, pricing, rate limits, and license/ToS constraints, with a recommended source stack
research.summary: The research splits the sources into two legal classes, and the architecture should follow that split. Proprietary providers (Google, Cesium ion, Azure, Esri, Mapbox, MapTiler, Apple) all ban server-side caching, proxying, rehosting and serving many users from one account. Open datasets (Mapterhorn, AWS Terrain Tiles, Copernicus DEM, USGS 3DEP, national lidar, NAIP, OSM, Overture, MS/Google buildings, ESA WorldCover, Meta canopy height, EOX s2cloudless 2016) can be pre-processed, cached and served from a shared community server as long as attribution and share-alike terms are met. So the community server should only handle open data. Every proprietary layer has to be fetched by the user's own client with the user's own key (BYO key), and only kept in an HTTP-semantics cache that honors Cache-Control and the provider's TTL caps (Mapbox 30 days per device, Azure 6 months, Cesium only a general-purpose HTTP cache, Google whatever Cache-Control says). Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles is the only source that gives a real photoreal mesh worldwide, and it is cheap for one player. Billing counts root tileset requests: 1,000 free per month, then $6 per 1,000, and each root request allows at least 3 hours of unlimited tile requests. The legal limits are tight, though. There is no caching or offline use, no 'creating content' from the tiles, no use 'with or near a non-Google Map', you must show the Google Maps logo plus aggregated per-tile copyright text, and projects billed in the EEA get a 403 since 8 July 2025. Google's documents never mention games. Cesium for Unreal builds physics meshes from these tiles by default, so using them for collision has precedent, but it is still a gray area. Google's Elevation API is explicitly banned for building terrain models (Maps ToS 3.2.3(c)(iii)). Bing Maps is dead for new users: no new customers since 30 June 2024, free/basic keys stopped on 30 June 2025, and enterprise ends 30 June 2028. It is now only reachable through Cesium ion. Apple has no raw tile API, and its DPLA Attachment 6 forbids scraping and caching. For ground elevation the best fit is Mapterhorn (2025-26, open). I verified a public XYZ endpoint that serves Terrarium-encoded 512px WebP tiles, a 355.6 GB z0-12 planet PMTiles file, 458 regional files reaching z13-z18 from national lidar (about 9.9 TB in total), and 151 sources, all under open licenses. AWS Terrain Tiles (z15, frozen since 2017) is the fallback. Both are Web Mercator only (±85.05°), so the polar caps of a true spherical Earth need EPSG:4326 sources such as Copernicus GLO-30/90 COGs or Cesium World Terrain. For imagery, free and open options are coarse or regional: EOX s2cloudless is 10 m (the 2016 edition is CC BY, 2017-2025 is CC BY-NC-SA) and has a WGS84 matrix set; NAIP gives US 30-60 cm; national orthophotos cover some countries. High-resolution global imagery for a BYO key is best from Esri World Imagery through ArcGIS Location Platform (2M basemap tiles per month free, then $0.15 per 1,000, and E300 footnote 97 explicitly expects end users to create their own Location Platform keys for third-party apps) or Mapbox Satellite (750k raster tiles per month free). For buildings and roads, Overture (monthly, ODbL, GeoParquet on S3/Azure, with height, floor count, roof shape, roof direction, materials and colors, plus transportation segments) and OSM are the backbone. The public Overpass and OSMF tile servers are not meant for app backends (Overpass allows about 10k requests and 1 GB per day per user; tile servers ban prefetch and offline use), so the server should hold its own extracts, such as Protomaps planet PMTiles (about 120 GB, z15) or Overture/Geofabrik. Vegetation can come from ESA WorldCover 10 m plus Meta/WRI canopy height (about 1 m, CC BY 4.0) and OSM landuse. Microsoft Planetary Computer's STAC and data API are live with 138 collections (cop-dem-glo-30, nasadem, naip, esa-worldcover, sentinel-2-l2a, 3dep-lidar-*, ms-buildings) and are a convenient back end for the server.

findings.claim: Google Map Tiles API general caching rule: 'you must not pre-fetch, index, store, or cache any Content except under the limited conditions stated in the terms'. 'Offline uses' are listed as prohibited. Clients must honor Cache-Control (max-age, stale-while-revalidate, must-revalidate, private) and ETag.
findings.evidence: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/policies (section 'Pre-fetching, caching, or storage of content', last updated 2026-10-07). The Service Specific Terms (https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms/maps-service-terms) contain no Map Tiles section, so the general ToS 3.2.3(b) 'No Caching' applies.

findings.claim: Google Maps Platform ToS 3.2.3 forbids: (a) scraping, including 'pre-fetch, index, store, reshare, or rehost Google Maps Content outside the services' and bulk downloading tiles or elevation values; (c) creating content from Google content, e.g. '(iii) build terrain models based on elevation values from the Elevation API'; (e) 'No Use With Non-Google Maps ... will not use the Google Maps Core Services with or near a non-Google Map'. Map Tiles API is listed as a Core Service, so (e) applies to it.
findings.evidence: https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms section 3.2.3 (downloaded and grepped). Core Services list: https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms/maps-services (includes 'Map Tiles API', 'Elevation API').

findings.claim: Google explicitly allows hybrid scenes: Photorealistic 3D Tiles 'as background filler' combined with your own models in the foreground, if the UI says which parts come from Google. You may overlay your own 3D objects 'as long as the 3D objects aren't extracted, traced, or otherwise derived by hand or machine from Photorealistic 3D Tiles'. Third-party renderers may be used, but the renderer's logo must not overlap the Google logo or attributions.
findings.evidence: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/policies sections 'Display logo and data attributions in hybrid visualizations', 'Geodata overlays with Photorealistic 3D Tiles', 'Display the Google Maps logo with third-party renderers'.

findings.claim: Google 3D Tiles protocol: root is GET https://tile.googleapis.com/v1/3dtiles/root.json?key=KEY. Child URIs are relative, carry a 'session' parameter, and need the key appended to every request. Tiles are .json sub-tilesets and .glb. The per-tile glTF asset.copyright must be aggregated, sorted by occurrence and shown on one line. The documentation's sample glTF has generator 'draco_decoder', so a Draco decoder is required.
findings.evidence: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/create-renderer (sample URLs .../datasets/CgA/files/UlRPVEYuYnVs.json?session=CIqhrPOFvdHSYg&key=KEY and ...UlRPVEYubm9k.glb?...).

findings.claim: Google pricing and quotas: Photorealistic 3D Tiles is an Enterprise SKU with 1,000 free events per month, then $6.00 per 1,000 up to 100k. Billing and quota count root tileset requests only: 'Tile requests for Photorealistic 3D Tiles don't impact your daily quota'. One root request gives at least 3 hours of renderer tile requests. Limits are 10,000 root requests per day and 12,000 tile requests per minute. 2D Map Tiles: 100,000 free per month, then $0.60 per 1,000, with default quotas of 6,000 per minute and 15,000 per day.
findings.evidence: https://developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/pricing ; https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/usage-and-billing (downloaded text).

findings.claim: EEA billing addresses: since 8 July 2025, Photorealistic 3D Tiles and 2D satellite tiles are not returned and requests get HTTP 403 ('Photorealistic 3D tiles are not available').
findings.evidence: https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/map-tiles ; EEA notices on every Map Tiles doc page.

findings.claim: Google's documentation never mentions games. The 3D Tiles FAQ says the tiles are for 'immersive visualizations', and 'programmatically reading and recording measurements (heights, distances, elevations, etc.)' counts as derivative and is prohibited. Building BeamNG collision from the mesh is therefore a gray area. Cesium for Unreal does create physics meshes from Google tiles by default ('Create Physics Meshes'), and Cesium staff recommend it for driving, so there is precedent for runtime physics.
findings.evidence: https://mapsplatform.google.com/resources/blog/commonly-asked-questions-about-our-recently-launched-photorealistic-3d-tiles/ ; Cesium forum threads e.g. https://community.cesium.com/t/google-photorealistic-3d-tiles-turn-off-collision/30351 (staff replies; anecdotal).

findings.claim: Cesium ion plans: Community (free, non-commercial) gives 10 GB storage, 15 GB streaming per month, 1,000 Global Imagery sessions (Bing/Google/Azure) and 1,000 Google 3D root tiles per month. Commercial is $149/mo for 150 GB streaming. ToS 2.2.2 says you may not store Cesium Data Output for offline use, but 'client-side and proxy-based caching are allowed as long as it is a general caching mechanism for performance that caches other internet traffic as well'. 2.2.1 says Licensed Services 'may not be operated ... as, or to perform, a service for or on behalf of any third parties'.

findings.claim: Cesium World Terrain is quantized-mesh 1.0. Resolution: about 30-90 m between 60°S and 60°N, 1-2 m in England, 50 cm on the US West Coast, 1-30 m elsewhere in the US, 5 m in Australia, 8 m in New Zealand, 1 km for the whole Earth. Ion asset IDs: OSM Buildings 96188, Google P3DT 2275207 (from CesiumJS source). World Terrain=1 and Bing Aerial=2 are the known defaults but were not re-checked here.

findings.claim: Esri World Imagery: the tiling goes to LOD 23 (0.0187 m/px tiling resolution). Credit is 'Esri, Vantor, Earthstar Geographics, and the GIS User Community'. The item license is the Esri Master License Agreement, and the layer 'is not intended to be used to export tiles for offline'. ArcGIS Location Platform gives 2M basemap tiles free, then $0.15 per 1,000. E300 footnote 10: 'Programmatic use of session tokens (e.g., exporting volumes of basemap tiles) is not permitted'. Footnote 97: end users prompted for an API key by a third party's app 'must generate such API keys through an ArcGIS Location Platform', which explicitly supports the BYO-key model. The legacy keyless endpoint server.arcgisonline.com still returns tiles (HTTP 200), but licensed use needs a Location Platform key; ibasemaps-api rejects requests without a token.

findings.claim: Mapbox Product Terms (21 July 2026): §2.8.1 allows on-device caching of Mapping API content for up to 30 days on the device that made the request, and the customer 'shall not distribute Licensed Map Content, including from a cache, by proxying'. §1.9 requires queries only in response to human interaction, with no bulk or automated queries, no scraping, and no export/cache/store except as permitted. §1.6 bans tracing or deriving data except tracing satellite imagery for non-commercial use or for OSM. §1.2.2 requires an extra license for 'vehicle usage', defined as apps used within vehicles or vehicle systems; a desktop game is probably outside that definition (inference). blockers: Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles cannot go through a shared community server. ToS 3.2.3(a) bans storing, resharing or rehosting, and 3.2.3(b) bans caching beyond Cache-Control. Each user must fetch directly from Google with their own key and billing account (the Demo Key does not cover Map Tiles).
Google 3D Tiles and 2D satellite tiles return 403 for EEA-billed projects since 8 July 2025, so the photoreal layer is unavailable to European users who bill there.

Google ToS 3.2.3(e) 'No Use With Non-Google Maps' applies to Map Tiles API as a Core Service. Mixing Google tiles with Esri or Mapbox imagery or an OSM-derived 'map' in the same view is legally risky. Google's policy only explicitly allows Google tiles as background with your own foreground models and clear attribution.

Collision geometry derived from Google meshes is a gray area. The FAQ calls programmatic measurement of heights or elevations 'derivative and prohibited', and the policy bans 'Geodata extraction'. Safest design: Google tiles are visual only and physics comes from open DEM and OSM data.
Google Elevation API is explicitly banned for terrain models (3.2.3(c)(iii)), so it cannot be a DEM source.
Bing Maps for Enterprise accepts no new customers (since June 2024), free keys died 30 June 2025, and enterprise ends 30 June 2028. It is only reachable through Cesium ion's metered imagery sessions.
Apple Maps provides no raw tile or 3D access, and the DPLA forbids scraping and caching. Not usable.

Proprietary BYO-key providers (Esri, Mapbox, Azure, MapTiler, Cesium ion) all forbid serving many users from one key or cache. Mapbox allows a 30-day cache per device and no proxying; Azure allows at most 6 months and not to scale to multiple users; Cesium allows only a general-purpose HTTP cache; MapTiler forbids a server-side cache.

Several 'free' tiers are non-commercial: Cesium ion Community, MapTiler Free, EOX s2cloudless 2017-2025 (CC BY-NC-SA, share-alike), and OSM US tiles. The mod must stay non-commercial (no paid tiers or Patreon-gated features), or buy licenses.

OSM public infrastructure (Overpass, tile.openstreetmap.org, vector.openstreetmap.org) explicitly forbids app back ends, prefetch, bulk and offline use. A real deployment needs self-hosted OSM or Overture extracts.

Most open raster tilesets (Mapterhorn, AWS Terrain Tiles, Google 2D, Esri, Mapbox, Azure) are Web Mercator and stop at ±85.05°. A true spherical Earth needs EPSG:4326 sources for the polar caps: Copernicus GLO-30/90 COGs, EOX WGS84 matrix set, Cesium World Terrain (geographic TMS), or Google 3D Tiles (ECEF).

Data volume for a self-hosted open server is large: Mapterhorn is about 9.9 TB in total (355.6 GB for z0-12), Protomaps planet about 120 GB, and Overture buildings are large (size not verified). Lazy on-demand fetching from source buckets or PMTiles range requests is needed instead of a full mirror.

The global DEM baseline (Copernicus GLO-30, used by Mapterhorn and Cesium) is a DSM, so roofs and tree canopy are baked into the heights outside lidar areas. The server must flatten under roads and buildings or use DTM where available.
recommendations: Split the system into two strictly separate pipelines. (1) An 'open data' server, local or community, that may fetch, pre-process, cache and serve: Mapterhorn, AWS Terrain Tiles, Copernicus DEM, USGS 3DEP, national lidar, NAIP, EOX 2016 (or 2017-2025 for non-commercial only), Overture, OSM, MS/Google buildings, WorldCover, canopy height. (2) A 'BYO-key' client fetcher running on the user's machine, the local companion process counts as the user's own client, that calls proprietary APIs directly with the user's key. Its only disk cache follows HTTP semantics and per-provider TTL caps: honor Cache-Control for Google, at most 30 days for Mapbox, at most 6 months for Azure, a general HTTP cache for Cesium. Never share that cache between users.

Ground elevation: use Mapterhorn as the primary source (https://tiles.mapterhorn.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp, Terrarium, up to z17-18 in lidar countries, 30 m elsewhere). On a community server, mirror or range-read its PMTiles instead of hammering the XYZ endpoint. Fall back to AWS Terrain Tiles z15. For polar caps above 85°, and as an ellipsoid-native source, read Copernicus GLO-30/90 COGs server-side. Cesium World Terrain via the user's own ion token is optional.

Ground texture: build the shipped default only from open sources. Far LOD: EOX s2cloudless (WGS84 matrix set for the poles; the 2016 CC BY layer if any commercial angle exists). Near LOD: NAIP (US) and national open orthophotos. Make it look good up close with procedural material splatting driven by ESA WorldCover and OSM landuse, because even 30 cm imagery looks blurry at car height. Offer optional BYO-key high-res imagery: Esri World Imagery through the user's own ArcGIS Location Platform key (2M tiles per month free; E300 footnote 97 supports end-user keys) or Mapbox Satellite (750k per month free). Keep these client-side only, with the required attribution on screen.

Buildings: use Overture buildings (which already merge OSM, Microsoft, Google and Esri) with height, num_floors, roof_shape, roof_direction and colors/materials for procedural extrusion and roofs. Pre-tile them server-side into a compact per-tile mesh or JSON format. Meet ODbL: attribution, and offer the derived database if it is distributed publicly (rendered meshes count as a Produced Work).

Roads: use Overture transportation segments (or OSM PBF via a Geofabrik or planet extract) processed server-side into road splines and meshes with width from lanes/class, bridge/tunnel layering and speed limits. Never use public Overpass at runtime except for tiny debug queries with a proper User-Agent.
Vegetation: place instanced trees from ESA WorldCover classes, Meta/WRI canopy height (density and height), and OSM natural=wood/tree_row/tree nodes.

Optional photoreal mesh near the player: make Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles opt-in with the user's own Google key, fetched directly from tile.googleapis.com. It is cheap for one player: 1,000 free root requests per month, and each covers at least 3 h of unlimited tile requests. Implement 3D Tiles traversal with Draco decoding, session-parameter propagation, and an on-screen Google Maps logo plus aggregated per-tile copyright. Treat it as visual only, with collision from DEM and OSM proxies. Don't show other providers' imagery in the same view while it is active. Detect HTTP 403 (EEA) and fall back gracefully. Cesium ion asset 2275207 is an alternative path for users without a Google billing account, subject to the same Google terms.

Keep the mod non-commercial and open source. Several free tiers and licenses depend on it (Cesium Community, EOX NC-SA, MapTiler Free, OSM US). Ship an attribution panel that builds itself from the active layers (Mapterhorn attribution.json, ODbL '© OpenStreetMap contributors', Overture, EOX string, Esri/Mapbox/Google strings).

Before building the Google layer, test with a real key: record the Cache-Control and ETag headers on root.json and .glb responses, the glTF extensions used (Draco, texture formats), and bandwidth per minute of driving. Consider emailing Google Maps Platform support to ask whether real-time vehicle simulation in a game counts as allowed 'map visualization'.

Use Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC and its data API as a convenient server-side back end for Copernicus DEM, NASADEM, NAIP, WorldCover, Sentinel-2 and 3DEP lidar instead of mirroring them, after checking its rate limits.

The same pattern is in techCore.lua:283-307, proceduralPrimitives.lua:671, procTrack.lua:195 and splineTrack.lua:390/983. verifications.claim: Structure of the createMesh argument: the outer array is a list of detail levels, and each entry is a list of submeshes {verts, uvs, normals, faces{v,n,u} 0-based, material}.
verifications.evidence: Resolves the 'LODs vs submesh groups' question. roadArchitect/roadMesh.lua:353 calls createMesh({ { surfaceMeshSW, endCapsSW } }): one outer entry holding two submeshes with different materials. segmentToProceduralMesh.lua:24-26,37 passes {meshes1, meshes1, meshes1}, where each entry is compileMeshInfo's list of submeshes (:76-83). That is 3 identical detail levels, the shape of a LOD chain. planet.lua:226-241 shows the faces {v=,u=,n=} format with vec3 normals. The LOD switch thresholds are not verified.

verifications.claim: Static collision is one global structure rebuilt in full by be:reloadCollision(), with no incremental add/remove exposed to Lua, and the rebuild blocks the frame for 0.05-2.4 s.
verifications.evidence: Global rebuild: confirmed. The be bindings list only reloadCollision, reloadStaticCollision and setDynamicCollisionEnabled (exe strings 201067-201081); no per-object add exists, and Lua never calls reloadStaticCollision. One nuance on blocking: libbeamng builds StaticCollider::build_kdtree and refreshTree with std::async/parallel_for (lib strings 4218-4243). In beamng.3.log:9834-9843, 'Physics collision reloaded in 0.054s' is logged at 962.05, GE Lua keeps logging (flowgraph build at 962.0516-962.0527), and '*** Loaded Static Collision in 0.333s' only arrives at 962.39. So the kd-tree build can finish asynchronously after the GE thread resumes. In other cases (983.92) it is reported inside the reload. The GE-side stall is roughly the instance-generation time (0.05-0.87 s), and the kd-tree takes about 0.07 s for 2M tris, 0.35 s for 9M and 1.6 s for 37M. What physics does during the async window is unknown.

verifications.claim: Runtime Material creation with a colorMap texture works, including textures downloaded at runtime.

Pointing colorMap at a freshly written /temp/beamngEarth/*.dds is unverified but highly plausible, since the VFS serves the user folder. The CEF CSP limits connect-src to localhost. A companion process is therefore mandatory.

verifications.evidence: wsUtils.lua:27-29 ('the server is serviced by its own thread (webServer.cpp) ... read the server's mutex-protected event queue'), :67-75 (bind forced to 127.0.0.1 under the network sandbox). mcp/server.lua:109-116 uses BNGWebWSServer.getOrCreate('127.0.0.1', PORT, ...) plus enableHttpHandler. Rally client.lua uses socket.http to localhost, which is blocking. Binary-safety and size limits of WS messages are UNVERIFIED, so send bulk data as files.

verifications.claim: Scene objects use float32 positions, and the engine has no runtime floating origin. The '500 km shift' flag the devs mentioned is a runtime origin shift.
verifications.evidence: Float32 scene and no runtime rebasing: CONFIRMED (Point3F/TransformF bindings; cameraUpdate.lua:145-146 'jumps on the floating point grid' vs getRefNodeAbsPositionXYZ 'double precision grid'). The '500 km' facility is the load-time flag -levelOffset x y z: parseArgs.lua:119-131 → server.setLevelOffset → server.lua:61-83 patchLoadingContext sets ldgCtx.tileTransform once at level load. It is a static offset and cannot rebase at runtime, so the mod must do its own rebasing. It is, however, a ready-made harness for measuring physics and render precision at 100-1000 km.

verifications.claim: A whole vehicle can be moved without a physics reset (for rebasing), keeping its velocity.
verifications.evidence: veh:setClusterPosRelRot(refNodeOr-1, x,y,z, qx,qy,qz,qw). spawn.lua:532-535 follows it with applyClusterVelocityScaleAdd(...,0,0,0,0) to zero velocity explicitly, and techCore.lua:909-915 (BeamNGpy teleport with reset=false) calls setClusterPosRelRot WITHOUT zeroing. Both imply velocity is preserved by default. Exact angular-velocity and rotation-of-velocity semantics, and coupled-trailer behaviour, are unverified.

verifications.claim: Gravity direction is controllable: uniform scalar along Z, plus additive point-mass planets.
verifications.evidence: core/environment.lua:1194-1212 setGravity writes LevelInfo.gravity and queues obj:setGravity(g) to all vehicles (a scalar along world Z only). Vehicle beamstate.lua:592-663 setPlanets with 5 numbers per planet. directionalGravity.lua:55-80 fakes an arbitrary gravity direction with a planet 1,000 km away. funstuff.lua:120-141 adds a repulsive planet without touching uniform gravity, which strongly implies planets ADD to uniform gravity (zero it with setGravity(0) for pure radial gravity). Uniform -Z is sufficient inside a re-centred ENU bubble.

verifications.claim: Terrain can be modified at runtime, and several TerrainBlocks can provide physics at the same time.
verifications.evidence: Runtime modification is CONFIRMED: terrainGenerator.lua:172-182,463 (TerrainBlock(), importMaps), terrainEditor.lua:1222-1266 (importMaps on an existing block), terraform.lua (setHeightGrid + updateGrid), and setPosition followed by reloadCollision (terrainGenerator.lua:98-103). Multi-block physics is UNVERIFIED and probably unsupported: libbeamng strings speak of a single 'heightmap buffer' / 'sent height map data' / 'layer map buffer' (lib strings 4249-4253), and core/terrain.lua returns only the first block. The block is flat and axis-aligned, between 128² and 8192².

verifications.claim: Far, render-only tiles can be kept out of the collision rebuild.
verifications.evidence: TSStatic collisionType='None' does this reliably. ProceduralMesh has no collisionType field (no such docstring near its strings). SceneObject:enableCollision()/disableCollision() exist (exe 202015-202016) and are used in gizmo.lua:104/163 and aiViz.lua:293 to hide objects from raycasts. Whether they also exclude an object from the physics static-collision rebuild is untested. This decides whether far LOD should be ProceduralMesh or TSStatic+.dae.

contradictions_resolved: Shape of the createMesh outer array (runtime-meshes: list of LODs; mod-structure: unclear). Resolved: the outer array is the detail-level list and each element is a list of submeshes. roadMesh.lua:353 builds one level with 2 submeshes and 2 materials; trackBuilder passes 3 identical submesh lists as 3 levels (segmentToProceduralMesh.lua:24-26,37). LOD switch distances remain untested.

Can Lua fetch from the internet? mod-structure and existing-tools said luasocket/luasec https could reach tile servers; io-networking said no. Resolved as NO. The exe holds the luasocket_sandbox host allowlist (strings 191384-191394), and LuaSec cannot load because luaopen_ssl_config is missing while ssl.lua:11 requires it. Even with the sandbox off there is no TLS. The companion process is mandatory.

Retail sandbox state. io-networking's disassembly says the sandbox is forced on unless tech state is 7, but wsUtils.lua:72-74 says 'The Sandbox.Network API only exists on tech/Aegis builds, so a missing API means no sandbox'. Not resolvable statically, and moot for the design: assume a loopback-only (or LAN) companion. A runtime probe through MCP run_lua will settle it.

'BeamNG added a flag to shift the world 500 km' (existing-tools) vs 'no origin-shift facility' (world-physics). Resolved: the flag is -levelOffset x y z (parseArgs.lua:119-131, server.lua:61-83). It applies a static tileTransform at level load and is not a runtime floating origin. The mod must rebase itself, and the flag is useful for precision testing at 100/500/1000 km.

Spherical-world approach. mod-structure suggested planet.lua's cube-sphere plus setPlanets radial gravity; world-physics and existing-tools suggested a flat ENU bubble with -Z gravity. Resolved for the ENU bubble: a planet-centred scene puts every coordinate near 6.37e6 m (float32 ULP 0.5 m). setPlanets is additive (funstuff.lua) and can stay as an optional experiment. In the bubble the error from uniform gravity is d/R (0.07° at 8 km).

Drivable ground near the player. The terrain report recommends one recentred TerrainBlock; the other reports recommend ProceduralMesh. Resolved for v1: ProceduralMesh tiles. Both paths need be:reloadCollision after a move or reimport. A TerrainBlock is single-block, axis-aligned, max 8192², has a texture-pack cache (temp/art/terrainmaterialcache) and probably a single physics heightmap buffer (libbeamng strings). ProceduralMesh tiles allow arbitrary tile shapes, direct per-tile DDS imagery and a ring of tiles. Keep TerrainBlock as an A/B experiment, because heightfield collision does not inflate the kd-tree.

reloadCollision 'blocks for 0.05-2.4 s' (runtime-meshes, terrain). Refined: the log shows the GE-side 'Physics collision reloaded' cost is instance generation, while the kd-tree build (std::async/parallel_for in libbeamng) sometimes completes about 0.33 s after GE resumes (beamng.3.log:9837 vs the 962.39 'Loaded Static Collision'). Cost scales with triangle count: about 0.07 s for 2M tris on this machine. With an empty level and a small collidable ring (≤1-2M tris) the hitch should be well under 100 ms.

Floating-origin rebase radius (2-5 km vs 4-8 km vs 10-20 km). Resolved: every rebase costs a full collision rebuild plus a navgraph rebuild, so fewer rebases are better. Float32 ULP is 0.5 mm at 8 km and 1 mm at 16 km, and BeamNG physics is vehicle-local (estama) and was stabilised around v0.34. Start at 8 km and raise it after -levelOffset precision tests.

Can glTF be loaded? (mod-structure: unverified; runtime-meshes: verified). Resolved: glTF works only with the -assimp flag (exe 194773, 202630-202631). Don't depend on it. Google tiles are ECEF and need re-anchoring to ENU anyway, so the companion transcodes everything.

Using Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles for collision (existing-tools cites Cesium for Unreal precedent; data-sources calls it a ToS gray area). Resolved for the design: Google is an optional, visual-only, BYO-key layer streamed by the user's local companion, which keeps only an HTTP-semantics cache and shows on-screen attribution. Physics always comes from open DEM and OSM/Overture.
gaps_answered: Excluding far tiles from collision: TSStatic collisionType='None' works for sure. ProceduralMesh has no collisionType field. disableCollision() exists on SceneObject but its effect on the physics rebuild is untested. Plan: far LOD as TSStatic(.dae, None), or test ProceduralMesh+disableCollision in phase 0.

Texture delivery: Lua has no in-memory texture upload, so textures must be files in the VFS. The engine keeps PNG→DDS caches in /temp (resourceUtil.lua:1520), and the exe has convertToDDS. The companion should write mipmapped BC1/BC7 .dds under <user>/temp/beamngEarth/ to avoid in-game decode and compression.

Where bulk files go: the user folder ~/.local/share/BeamNG/BeamNG.drive/current/temp/ is the VFS /temp/. The engine itself reads and writes caches there (temp/art/terrainmaterialcache/*.dds exists on disk). Write-then-rename, plus versioned filenames because resources are cached by path.

Is the collision rebuild truly blocking? Partly asynchronous: the kd-tree is built with std::async/parallel_for (libbeamng strings 4218-4243), and GE resumes before it finishes in some cases (beamng.3.log:9837-9843).
Precision test harness: launch with -levelOffset 500000 0 0 (parseArgs.lua:119) on smallgrid or our level to measure collision and render jitter far from the origin before choosing the rebase radius.

Vehicle rebase primitive: setClusterPosRelRot without velocity zeroing (techCore.lua:909-915), plus setOriginalTransform. Pausing physics around a rebase is advisable because tile moves (GE) and vehicle moves (physics queue) land on different ticks and collision must be rebuilt.

Gravity semantics: planets add to uniform gravity (funstuff.lua:120-141 does not zero it), and directional gravity is emulated with a distant planet (directionalGravity.lua:55-80). Uniform -Z is the v1 choice.

Dev and test loop: the built-in MCP server exists (lua/ge/extensions/mcp/server.lua binds 127.0.0.1:29292/mcp, with tools in mcp/tools/*.lua). The game is not running now, so no live tests were possible. Enabling Options > Advanced > MCP lets every phase-0 probe run automatically.
Mod loading: modmanager.lua:704-711 dofile()s every /scripts/**/modScript.lua. Confirmed pattern: setExtensionUnloadMode + extensions.load('beamngEarth_core').

The .cdae format is only partially documented (documentation.beamng.com/modding/file_formats/cdae/): the nodes/objects/details structs and collision meshes are not described. Writing .cdae directly is risky. Write .dae (the engine auto-caches .cdae) or use ProceduralMesh.

Starting the companion: the mod cannot launch it (os.execute/io.popen are sandboxed, per the libbeamng strings 'Lua tried to execute system command'). The user starts it, for example via a Steam launch option `earthd & %command%` or a systemd user unit. The mod shows a 'companion not connected' UI state.

Ocean: WaterPlane is flat and infinite. Inside the bubble that is fine (drop 7.8 cm at 1 km, 7.8 m at 10 km), but far ocean must be part of the curved LOD meshes, and the WaterPlane should be disabled or limited when the curved ocean shows.
remaining_unknowns: Does ProceduralMesh get physics collision without be:reloadCollision (via its internal updatePhysicsCollision)? What do the two booleans in be:reloadCollision(a,b) and be:reloadStaticCollision do (possibly a cheaper path)?
Does SceneObject:disableCollision() exclude a ProceduralMesh from the physics static-collision rebuild?
What does physics do during the asynchronous kd-tree build window (old tree, no collision, or a physics stall)? What is the real frame hitch with 0.5-2M collidable tris in an otherwise empty level?
ProceduralMesh vertex/index limits per submesh, LOD switch thresholds, and createMesh wall time and GC cost for a 257² grid built from Lua tables.
Do files written at runtime into /temp by an external process (DDS, DAE, materials.json) load immediately, or do they need FS:triggerFilesChanged? Does TSStatic DAE loading stall the main thread?
Collision and render precision at 20/100/500 km from the origin (test with -levelOffset), which sets the rebase radius.
setClusterPosRelRot behaviour with a non-identity rotation (are velocities rotated?), with coupled trailers, and with detached parts (-1 vs refNode).
Binary-safety and maximum message size of BNGWebWSServer data frames, and the peer event types for connect/disconnect.
Actual retail state of Engine.Sandbox.Lua/Network, and whether LAN hosts are reachable by a luasocket client.
Practical maxima for LevelInfo.visibleDistance (50-150 km), depth precision (is reversed-Z on by default under Vulkan?), and shadow and LOD cost at that range.
Whether the physics core collides with more than one TerrainBlock (only matters if the TerrainBlock A/B path is pursued).
Google Map Tiles legal questions: games, the 'No use with non-Google maps' clause when open terrain fills the distance, Cache-Control TTLs, and EEA billing for this user.
Memory and VRAM budget per tile and the scene-object count limits before render and simtime degrade (hundreds of ProceduralMesh/TSStatic objects plus materials).
critique.architecture:
"Globe in the companion, flat bubble in the game" (the MSFS anchor-space / Cesium origin-shift pattern), split into two processes.

1) COMPANION 'earthd'. Rust for production; a Python prototype is fine for phase 1. It runs on 127.0.0.1:47613, or on the LAN, and owns all internet access, geodesy and heavy work.
(a) Geodesy core in f64: WGS84 geodetic↔ECEF↔ENU(anchor).
(b) Global tile index with no polar warping: an S2-style cube-sphere quadtree (6 faces with the quadratic warp, levels ~L8 at 40 km down to ~L17 at 70 m) for everything it synthesises. Web-Mercator sources (Mapterhorn/Terrarium DEM, Esri/EOX imagery) are resampled into cube-sphere tiles. EPSG:4326 sources (Copernicus GLO-30 COGs, EOX WGS84 matrix set) cover the polar caps above 85°. ECEF-native sources such as optional Google 3D Tiles are consumed as-is.
(c) Fetchers with two strictly separated caches: a shareable cache for open data (Mapterhorn, AWS Terrarium, Copernicus, Overture/OSM extracts such as Protomaps or Geofabrik PMTiles, ESA WorldCover, EOX s2cloudless-2016) and a private HTTP-semantics cache for BYO-key data (Esri Location Platform, Mapbox, Google).
(d) Builders per tile: an adaptive terrain mesh (RTIN/Martini or a regular grid simplified with meshoptimizer) with skirts and DSM flattening under OSM roads and buildings; imagery mosaics encoded as mipmapped BC1/BC7 DDS; extruded Overture/OSM buildings (box or simple roofs, with simplified collision hulls near the player); road ribbons draped on the DEM; navgraph node tables from OSM/Overture transportation.
(e) Output: files written atomically (write then rename) into <user>/temp/beamngEarth/<session>/<tileId>_<ver>.{bin, dds, dae, materials.json}. A small JSON control channel says 'tile ready', 'unload' and 'rebase ack'.

2) MOD 'beamng_earth.zip', developed unpacked in mods/unpacked/.
- A level levels/beamng_earth/ built from the smallgrid skeleton without GroundPlane: SpawnSphere, LevelInfo (gravity -9.81, visibleDistance 30-60 km raised at runtime, nearClip 0.1), ScatterSky with its planet-radius atmosphere, TimeOfDay, CloudLayer.
- scripts/beamng_earth/modScript.lua → extensions.load('beamngEarth_core').
- Lua modules: net (BNGWebWSServer or luasocket TCP with settimeout(0) and a frame budget); anchor (doubles: φ0, λ0, h0 and the ECEF↔ENU matrices); tiles (spawn and delete queue, time-sliced at about 2 ms per frame); collision scheduler; rebase; navgraph (map.reset(customNodes)); sky (core_celestial.setLocation from the player's lat/lon); UI (teleport to lat/lon, companion status, auto-built attribution panel); optional MCP dev tools.

COORDINATES. The game frame is ENU at anchor A: +X east, +Y north, +Z up along the ellipsoid normal. Each tile's mesh vertices are float32 offsets from that tile's ENU(A) origin o_t, computed exactly in f64 on the server as ENU_A(P) - o_t. Because every point is the true ellipsoid point expressed in A's axes, curvature (d²/2R) and correct geometry everywhere, poles included, come out automatically. The scene never sees a coordinate beyond about 10-20 km plus the LOD horizon.
FLOATING ORIGIN. When the player's double-precision position (getRefNodeAbsPositionXYZ) is more than R_rebase (start at 8 km, tune after -levelOffset tests) from A, rebase:
1. Pause physics.
2. Compute the new anchor A' and the rigid transform T = ENU_A'∘ENU_A⁻¹. This is a translation plus a rotation of about d/R, roughly 0.07° at 8 km.
3. Apply T to every tile object with setTransform, to every vehicle with setClusterPosRelRot(-1,...) plus setOriginalTransform, and to the camera, recovery points and DecalRoads.
4. Rebuild the navgraph, call be:reloadCollision() once, and resume physics.
5. Fire an onEarthOriginShift hook, and tell the companion to emit new tiles in A' from then on (existing tiles stay valid thanks to their transforms).
Gravity stays uniform -Z, which is correct within the bubble. setPlanets remains a later 'true radial gravity' experiment.

LOD. Server-driven screen-space-error selection over the cube-sphere quadtree, using pose, fov and screen height sent at about 10 Hz: refine while geometricError*H/(dist*2tan(fov/2)) > 16-24 px. REPLACE refinement keeps the parent visible until all children are ready, and skirts hide cracks. Indicative rings:
- R0, 0-1 km: 1-2 m DEM, buildings, collidable.
- R1, 1-5 km: about 8 m.
- R2, 5-30 km: about 30-60 m.
- R3: about 250 m to the horizon, with a coarse globe at altitude.
Fog and the atmosphere hide the far edge.

COLLISION. Only R0 terrain tiles plus nearby buildings and bridges are collidable ProceduralMesh objects, at about 0.5-2M tris in total. Rebuild in batches when the R0 set changes (every ~250-500 m travelled), with tiles prebuilt ahead along the velocity vector so they are in place before the player arrives. R1+ tiles are render-only: TSStatic .dae with collisionType None, or ProceduralMesh with disableCollision if phase-0 tests show that excludes them. Material groundType comes from land cover or OSM (ASPHALT for roads, GRASS, DIRT, SAND).

DATA v1 (all open and cacheable):
- DEM: Mapterhorn as primary (Terrarium WebP z≤12 globally, up to z18 in lidar countries), AWS Terrarium z15 as fallback, Copernicus GLO-30 at the poles.
- Imagery: EOX s2cloudless-2016 (CC BY) at far LOD; NAIP and national orthophotos near the player; optional BYO-key Esri World Imagery near the player.
- Near-ground look: procedural detail from ESA WorldCover and OSM land use.
- Buildings and roads: Overture/OSM from self-held extracts (never public Overpass at runtime).
v2 adds an optional Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles visual layer: BYO key, visual-only, attribution on screen, no shared cache, and a fallback on HTTP 403 for EEA projects.
roadmap:
Phase 0, probes (1-2 weeks, with MCP enabled at 127.0.0.1:29292). Use run_lua scripts to measure and decide:
- Engine.Sandbox flags.
- luasocket and BNGWebWSServer round trips with NUL/0xFF payloads.
- Wall time and GC cost of createMesh on a 257² grid.
- be:reloadCollision timing at 0.5/1/2/5M tris in an empty level, and the hitch it causes.
- Whether a ProceduralMesh is drivable without a reload.
- Whether disableCollision excludes a mesh from the physics rebuild.
- That a .dds/.dae/.materials.json written by an external process into /temp loads right away.
- setClusterPosRelRot velocity behaviour, including with a trailer.
- Driving jitter at -levelOffset 20000/100000/500000.
- visibleDistance 50-100 km and depth artefacts.

Phase 1, skeleton:
- Mod zip, plus the beamng_earth level from the smallgrid skeleton without GroundPlane.
- The beamngEarth_core extension and a companion handshake over localhost.
- An anchor/ENU module in Lua doubles.
- A 'teleport to lat/lon' UI.
- core_celestial.setLocation following the player.
- Companion status and an attribution UI.

Phase 2, drivable terrain: the companion serves cube-sphere DEM tiles (Mapterhorn/Terrarium) as compact binary or .dae. The mod spawns the R0 collidable ProceduralMesh ring with flat-colour or WorldCover-based materials and schedules batched collision rebuilds. The floating-origin rebase is implemented and stress-tested.

Phase 3, LOD to the horizon: SSE quadtree rings R1-R3 as render-only tiles, parent-until-children-ready, skirts, curved ocean tiles, a fog and atmosphere tune, and imagery as DDS (EOX far, NAIP/orthophoto/BYO-key Esri near). Polar and antimeridian tests, for example driving at Svalbard and across the 180° meridian in Fiji.

Phase 4, man-made world: OSM/Overture roads as mesh ribbons or DecalRoads (overObjects=true) with DSM flattening, an AI navgraph through map.reset(customNodes) rebuilt on each region change and rebase, extruded buildings (collidable near the player, render-only far away), and per-surface groundType from OSM and land cover.

Phase 5, polish and performance: vegetation instancing from WorldCover, canopy height and OSM trees; a disk cache with LRU and quotas; streaming prediction along the velocity vector; VRAM and object budgets; traffic limited to the collidable area; replay disabled or converted to geodetic coordinates.

Phase 6, optional: a Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles visual layer (BYO key, Draco decode and ECEF→ENU on the server, aggregated copyright and logo on screen, HTTP-cache compliant, EEA 403 fallback); flight or altitude mode with a whole-globe view; experimental setPlanets radial gravity; a shared geodetic anchor protocol for multiplayer.
top_risks: Collision rebuild hitches. be:reloadCollision is the only static-collision API and rebuilds everything. If the GE-side stall of a 1-2M tri rebuild exceeds about 50-100 ms, streaming at highway speed stutters. Mitigations: a small collidable ring, simplified meshes, prebuilding ahead, rebuilds batched into moments like rebases, and a TerrainBlock heightfield as an A/B fallback.

LuaJIT mesh-building cost. createMesh takes nested Lua tables (one table per vertex and per face corner), so building tiles causes heavy GC churn on the single GE thread. Mitigations: time-slicing, coarse tiles, and moving render-only tiles to TSStatic .dae files the engine parses natively.

Rebase correctness. Every subsystem that stores absolute positions (vehicles, trailers, detached parts, camera smoothing, recovery points, navgraph and AI paths, traffic, decals and skidmarks, particles, triggers, replays) must shift together. Missed ones cause jumps or explosions. The ordering between moving GE objects and the physics-thread vehicle moves is also unproven.

Float32 precision far from the anchor. The rebase radius must be chosen from measured jitter (-levelOffset tests), not guesses. Visible distance of tens of km also stresses depth precision and LOD and shadow cost.

Legal and terms of service. Google tiles can't go through any shared server, can't be used for derived geometry such as collision, may conflict with mixing non-Google maps, and return 403 for EEA projects. Several 'free' sources are non-commercial or share-alike (EOX 2017+, Cesium Community). Keep the mod non-commercial and open source, and make the open-data pipeline the default.

Visual fidelity at car height. Open imagery is 10 m (Sentinel-2) outside the US and orthophoto countries, and Copernicus GLO-30 is a DSM, so roofs and canopy are baked into the ground. Roads will sit on trees unless the companion flattens under OSM roads and buildings, and expectations of 'Google Earth detail' may not be met without the BYO-key layers.

Undocumented engine behaviour and update fragility. VFS freshness of runtime-written files, ProceduralMesh limits, whether disableCollision affects physics, async kd-tree semantics and network-sandbox rules are all inferred from strings and logs, and a BeamNG update can change any of them. Keep a probe suite that runs over MCP after every game update.

Companion distribution and UX. Users must install and start a separate native process; the game sandbox prevents the mod from launching it. API keys and quotas belong to the user, and data volumes are large (Mapterhorn is about 9.9 TB in total), so on-demand range reads and a local cache are needed rather than mirrors.
